author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Florida Gators add Abdalla Youssef to men's swimming and diving roster
text:
The Florida men’s swimming and diving team announced on April 28 that Abdalla Youssef will join its roster for the 2026-27 season, according to head coach Anthony Nesty.
Youssef previously competed for Auburn University, where he was one of four swimmers representing the Tigers at the 2026 NCAA Championships. He participated in four events: the 100 butterfly, 200 butterfly, 800 freestyle relay, and 400 medley relay. During his freshman year at Auburn, Youssef earned All-American honors in each event he entered. He received honorable mention recognition for his performances in the 100 fly, 800 free relay, and 400 medley relay, and was named a first team All-American after reaching the finals in the 200 fly.
“Abdalla adds a strong competitive drive with valuable international and championship experience to our program,” Nesty said. “We’re excited to welcome him to the Gators and look forward to supporting his continued growth in and out of the pool. We can’t wait to see what he will accomplish with our program.”
Before joining collegiate swimming in the United States, Youssef represented Egypt at both the 20th and 21st World Aquatics Championships. There he set a national record for Egypt in the men’s 200-meter butterfly with a time of one minute, fifty-seven point eighty-five seconds.
Youssef joins an incoming class that includes transfer David Johnston as well as freshmen Santiago Alzate, Zoltan Bagi, Tai Pearson, and Liam Smith. When asked about his decision to attend Florida, Youssef said: “I chose the University of Florida because I’ve always liked the team culture and how everyone supports each other in the SEC and NCAA. Seeing the team push and motivate each other really inspired me. With the program’s history and great coaches, it was an easy decision to make… My goal is to become a professional athlete and be part of something bigger than myself. I believe being part of this team will help me reach my biggest goal of becoming an Olympic champion.”
